raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so I count every bag I buy, but I still do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If wheat or maize goes weak early, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer. I usually start from what I did last year and then look at what the better fields around me did. In Quzhou this wheat-maize rotation is common, so I will not do anything fancy. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the base fertilizer on before sowing, and give enough nitrogen to keep the stand thick. I have well water, so I will plan on 3 irrigations for wheat if the season is normal: one after sowing or at overwintering if needed, one at jointing, and one at filling. For maize, I will go with hybrid seed because that is what gives steadier yield here. After wheat harvest the time is tight, so I will keep maize simple and fast, mainly no-tillage direct sowing or very light surface work. I will keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, because with only 5 mu I can manage it by hand and I would rather spend some money than watch the crop turn pale. I also have some family labor but not everyone is home, so I will keep pesticide sprays to the key timings instead of too many passes.
